sources.fsa.health_fsa_limit: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf), retrieved 2026-10-11 s.3.15 (IRC 125(i)): $3,400; carryover $680
sources.debt_interest.mortgage_acquisition_cap: Statutory IRC 163(h)(3)(F); the $750,000 cap was made permanent by OBBBA s.70108. NOT indexed.
sources.passive_activity: Statutory IRC 469(i) ($25,000 allowance, $100k-$150k phase-out) and IRC 168 / 1250. NONE of these are inflation-indexed.
sources.retirement.uniform_lifetime_table: IRS Publication 590-B (2025), Appendix B Table III (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p590b.pdf), retrieved 2026-10-12. Life-expectancy tables were last revised effective 2022-01-01 and are NOT annually indexed.

_meta.verification_required: Sourced from primary documents, NOT yet signed off by the owner's CPA. `verified` stays false until then.
_meta.why_split_from_tax_tables: Deliberate: tax_tables holds rate SCHEDULES; this holds the thresholds statutory RULES test against. The rules (tax_wrappers.py, tax_debt_interest.py) are stable across years and need no re-verification; these amounts do.
unsourced_still: fsa.dependent_care_limit — OBBBA may have changed the $5,000 limit for 2026; NOT confirmed, left at the long-standing statutory $5,000 and flagged here rather than asserted.
retirement.rmd_age — 73 per SECURE 2.0 s.107 (rising to 75 in 2033); statutory, high confidence, not re-fetched.

hsa.note: Limits from Rev. Proc. 2025-19. The $1,000 catch-up is statutory (IRC 223(b)(3)) and NOT indexed.

retirement.note: Deduction phase-out RANGES are the IRC 219(g)(2)(A) width ($10,000; $20,000 joint) applied to the Notice 2025-67 start amounts. Roth ranges use the IRC 408A(c)(3)(A) width ($15,000; $10,000 joint); the joint 242,000-252,000 range is stated explicitly in the Notice.
retirement.uniform_lifetime_table_note: IRS Pub 590-B Appendix B, Table III (Uniform Lifetime) — the applicable denominator for an RMD. For unmarried owners, married owners whose spouse is not more than 10 years younger, and married owners whose spouse is not the sole beneficiary. Age 120 is '120 and over'. A spouse MORE than 10 years younger and sole beneficiary uses Table II (Joint and Last Survivor), which is not modelled — it gives a LONGER period and therefore a SMALLER RMD, so using this table for them overstates the forced distribution.
